summary: A trio MV in which each member plays a different unrequited status — the friend, the ex, the one being kept unofficial — and the comment section turns into a debate about which status hurts most. That argument is the single largest cluster and produces the most-liked non-celebrity comments, several of which lay out all three positions in structured form. The second cluster is acting praise, and it lands overwhelmingly on Dream: viewers who describe themselves as previously indifferent say she was the MVP, name her eyes and body language, and ask for her to be cast in a film. Natty's crying-while-eating-instant-noodles scene is singled out repeatedly. A third cluster is personal projection — viewers recount their own version of the same situation, one explaining why eating through tears is realistic. A smaller thread reads the sound as deliberately 90s Thai pop and welcomes the throwback, and a few English comments arrive via the Nadao actors and the director.

audience_signals: Giving each member a distinct role turns the comment section into an argument, and arguments produce the longest, most-liked comments — a reusable structural device
Dream is the member with the most upside from acting work: multiple commenters say this MV converted them from indifferent to fans and ask for casting
The audience reads the group as recording artists now, not YouTubers with a side project
Relationship-status framing is highly projectable — viewers slot their own history into the roles, which is why this format outperforms plain love songs on comment depth
A 90s Thai pop reference point pulls in an older listener segment who name the era unprompted
Guest actors' fandoms (Nadao) and the production crew bring a small English-language audience
